title: Nitrogenous fractions in perennial ryegrass across nitrogen-fertilizer treatments
journal: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
transcription_source: D. Pacheco and G. C. Waghorn (2008), Dietary nitrogen: definitions, digestion, excretion and consequences of excess for grazing ruminants
transcription_source_location: Table 3, page 110; table caption attributes the data to Goswami and Willcox (1969)
geography: Experimental location not established from the reviewed transcription source
material: Perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne) across four N-application rates, averaged across cuts at vegetative, heading, and flowering stages
measurement_method: The CSV transcribes total-N concentration and reported nitrogen-fraction percentages from Table 3 of the 2008 source; underlying 1969 methods were not reviewed from the primary full text.
evidence_class: Primary study values located through a secondary table transcription; class B source evidence with an explicit transcription chain
license: The CSV contains a limited numeric transcription and provenance. The 2008 article is available at the linked publisher site; source-specific reuse terms should be checked before redistribution.
activation_state: Reference-only. Not connected to GreenHub runtime parameters; N-basis fractions cannot be converted to molecule masses without further assumptions and a total-N/protein overlap reconciliation.
limitations: The source is fertilized cultivated ryegrass, not Dutch roadside grass or the VARTA project sample.
The reported values are averages over multiple growth stages and cuts, not stage-specific distributions.
Reported constituent fractions sum to less than 100 percent in each row; the residual column is arithmetic and is not a measured constituent.
Fraction values are percentages of total nitrogen, not mass percentages of the corresponding compounds.
This is a transcription from a 2008 secondary table; the original 1969 full text was not independently inspected.
